name: Katya Frei
text_en: Katya Frei was born in Belarus in 1994 and grew up in Polesia in the south-east of the country. She trained at the State College of Architecture and Construction in Minsk and studied graphics and printmaking at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, graduating in 2023. She works with lithography, woodcut, etching and drawing, often with plants and insects as motifs, and has lived and worked in Klagenfurt since 2023. In 2024 she received the third prize of the Nachwuchspreis Bildende Kunst Kärnten, funded by the Wietersdorfer Group.

name: Karlheinz Simonitsch
text_en: Karlheinz Simonitsch was born in Lienz, East Tyrol, in 1953, went to school in Klagenfurt, where Egon Wucherer was one of his teachers, and graduated from the University of Graz. He taught at the Handelsakademie Klagenfurt until 2003 and worked as a freelance artist with a studio in Klagenfurt; in 1995 he worked at the City of Klagenfurt's studio in Šmartno. From the 1990s he turned increasingly to sacred subjects and church interiors, working in drawing, watercolour, oil and mixed media as well as in glass and ceramics, for example the glass cross “Ich bin das Leben” (1998) in the parish church of Klagenfurt-Wölfnitz. He died in December 2015.

name: Ingrid Pröller
text_en: Ingrid Pröller was born in 1970 in Schärding, Upper Austria. From 1989 to 1997 she studied at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna and sports science in Vienna, with study stays at the École nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts in Paris (1995) and the Athens School of Fine Arts (1996–1997). She paints in oil and acrylic on canvas and regularly works on Crete, where she paints large panoramas outdoors. She lives and works in Vienna.

name: Alfred Scheikl
text_en: Alfred Scheikl was born in Klagenfurt in 1961. From 2012 to 2016 he studied painting at the Freie Akademie der Bildenden Künste Kärnten with Luka Anticevic, Peter Kohl, Rene Fadinger and Astrid Langer, followed by a master class with Luka Anticevic in 2016–2017. His paintings combine abstract and fractal elements. Since 2017 he has chaired the Kunstverein Velden, where he also teaches drawing and acrylic painting; he works in Klagenfurt.

name: Klaus Zlattinger
text_en: Klaus Zlattinger worked as an artist, art educator and gallerist; he died in December 2016. In 2026 the association kultur.im.puls marks the tenth anniversary of his death with the exhibition “Klaus Zlattinger & Friends” in the Galerie im Stiegenhaus in Seeboden.

name: Inge Lasser
text_en: Inge Lasser lives and works in Hermagor. She trained with Giselbert Hoke, Elvira Bach and Markus Lüpertz at the art academy in Bad Reichenhall. She joined postWERK in 2013 and is its secretary. She has exhibited in Austria, Germany, Italy and France, including the Galerie Offenes Atelier D.U.Design in Villach and the Kunstbahnhof Wörthersee in Velden.

name: Uwe Bressnik
text_en: Uwe Bressnik was born in Villach, Carinthia, in 1961 and studied at the University of Applied Arts Vienna from 1983 to 1989, graduating in Ernst Caramelle’s master class for graphic art. His work links visual art and music: in the series „Soul Source Records“ he makes hand-drawn records, record objects and sound rooms, and since about 2000 he has also performed as an improvising musician. He received the Carinthian Würdigungspreis for visual art in 2010 and lives and works in Vienna.

name: Franz Grabmayr
text_en: Franz Grabmayr was born in Obervellach, Carinthia, in 1927 and died in Vienna in 2015. He first worked as a teacher, studied at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna in the afternoons from 1954 and gave up teaching in 1964 to work only as an artist. He lived and painted in the northern Waldviertel, first at Schloss Rosenau and later on a farm near Zwettl, and spent the winters in a studio in the Karl-Marx-Hof in Vienna. His pictures are built up from very thick layers of paint; his subjects include fire, sand pits, mountain streams and dancers.

name: Inge Vavra
text_en: Inge Vavra was born in 1942 in Augsburg and grew up in Vienna. She graduated in graphic art and painting from the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna in 1965, also qualified as an art teacher, and has exhibited since 1964. In Carinthia she has carried out several art-in-architecture projects, among them works for the LKH Wolfsberg and the Pädagogische Hochschule in Klagenfurt, and in 2005 she received the Carinthian Würdigungspreis for visual art. She lives and works in Vienna and Krumpendorf.

name: Hans Kupelwieser
text_en: Hans Kupelwieser was born in Lunz am See, Lower Austria, in 1948. He trained at the Graphische Lehr- und Versuchsanstalt in Vienna (1970–73) and studied at the Hochschule für angewandte Kunst in Vienna (1976–82); from 1995 he held a professorship at the Institute of Contemporary Art at Graz University of Technology. His work, made since the late 1970s, consists mainly of sculpture and photography, including photograms, anodised aluminium reliefs and objects in stainless steel. He lives and works in Vienna and Lunz am See.

name: Walther Preiml
text_en: Walther Preiml is a printmaker and songwriter in Carinthia. After studying at the Landeskonservatorium Klagenfurt in 2003–2004, he came to art through photography in 2006 and took drawing lessons from 2007; since 2016 he has worked mainly in woodcut and paper-cut printing. Since 2010 he has performed his own songs in Carinthian dialect, and since 2022 he has worked as a freelance artist and songwriter, with his studio and home in Kötschach-Mauthen in the Gail Valley.

name: Margaretha Bauer
text_en: Margaretha Maria Bauer is vice president and treasurer of the Carinthian branch of the Berufsvereinigung der Bildenden Künstler Österreichs (BV Kärnten) and heads its gallery, the BV Galerie in Klagenfurt. She is a member of the Kunstverein Kärnten and in 2026 took part in its group exhibition "schmaler Grat" at the Künstlerhaus Klagenfurt.

name: Karl Bauer
text_en: Karl Bauer was born in Graz in 1905, grew up in Carinthia and studied painting at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna from 1925 to 1930 in the master class of Alois Delug. After years as a teacher in Vienna and Klosterneuburg, he worked from 1946 as a freelance painter and graphic artist in Klagenfurt, where he died in 1993. He painted mainly landscapes in oil and figure compositions, designed book covers and illustrations for the Eduard Kaiser publishing house, and made mosaics and stained-glass windows for Carinthian churches, among them the Stations of the Cross mosaics at the memorial on the Kreuzbergl in Klagenfurt (1959).

name: Eva Schlegel
text_en: Eva Schlegel was born in Hall, Austria, in 1960 and studied at the University of Applied Arts Vienna under Oswald Oberhuber from 1979 to 1985. From 1997 to 2006 she was professor of art and photography at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna. In photographs, objects and installations she examines the relationship between objects and perception. In 2011 she was commissioner of the Austrian Pavilion at the Venice Biennale; she lives and works in Vienna.

name: Adi Schmölzer
sources: “Adi Schmölzer verbindet Kunst und Jazz”, kaernten.orf.at, 5 March 2025
“Adi Schmölzer stellt in Sachsenburg aus”, okvolltreffer.at, 28 July 2025
text_en: Adi Schmölzer is a painter and architect from Upper Carinthia; he studied architecture, among others with Günther Domenig. His paintings, many of them large and made on the floor, mostly show women as figures in motion, and he usually listens to jazz while he paints. After years of work in Graz and Burgenland he returned to Carinthia and now lives in Spittal an der Drau, where the gallery iXart shows a permanent display of his work.

name: Inés Urach
text_en: Inés Urach studied at the Freie Akademie der Bildenden Künste in Klagenfurt from 2013 to 2017 and attended its master class with Luka Anticevic from 2018 to 2020. Before that she took painting courses at the European Art Academy in Trier (2005, 2006) and at the art academy in Bad Reichenhall (2011). Her abstract paintings deal with the relationship between paper and painting, with paper used as a material in the picture. Her studio is in the Europahaus in Klagenfurt.

name: Gudrun Zikulnig
text_en: Gudrun Zikulnig (née Juch) was born in Völkermarkt on 4 April 1965 and lives and works in Kühnsdorf. She graduated from the Freie Akademie für bildende Künste und Literatur Kärnten, with a master class under Luka Anticevic and Peter Kohl. She paints in oil and acrylic and works with collage, and teaches these techniques as a course instructor at the Kunstverein Velden. In 2012 she won a prize at the Ex Tempore in Grisignana.

name: Slava Mohl
text_en: Slava Mohl was born in Bosnia in 1978 and has lived in Austria since 1992. After training as a hotel and catering assistant she worked for several years as an office clerk; in 2016 she gave up that job to attend the master class for painting at the HTBLA Ortweinschule in Graz. Since then she has worked as a freelance painter, using pigment, chalk, paper and canvas. Her studio is in Deutsch Kaltenbrunn in Burgenland, and she has exhibited in Velden, Wolfsberg and Eisenstadt, among other places.

name: Epische Gemälde – Zwischen Mythos und Kosmos
sources: invitation and poster of the Galerie im Schloss Porcia
“‘Epische Gemälde | Zwischen Mythos und Kosmos’”, spittal-drau.at
text_en: Under the title “Epische Gemälde – Zwischen Mythos und Kosmos” (epic paintings – between myth and cosmos), Ingrid Pröller shows large-format paintings, some up to five metres wide, in the vaulted Salamancakeller of Schloss Porcia. The cycle runs from archaic landscapes to futuristic images and asks how people, nature and the cosmos relate. In “Wildes Kind” and “Kretische Landschaft” consumer waste intrudes on idyllic landscapes; “Geburt” and “Fabel” take up motifs of creation and storytelling. The poster image “Endzeit” (2022) reads a coastal scene with a child, an octopus and dead animals as a passage to a new beginning, and “Matrix” shows a cosmonaut as a modern Odysseus. Pröller, born in Schärding in 1970 and trained at the Akademie der bildenden Künste in Vienna, paints many of her works in an open-air studio on Crete.

name: Walther Preiml – Sehnsucht
text_en: Under the title “Sehnsucht” (longing), the printmaker and songwriter Walther Preiml, who lives in Kötschach-Mauthen, shows new work at the stARTup gallery. His woodcuts and frottages revolve around a “painful longing for the unattainable”; according to the ORF programme, the mountains of the region, seen from Preiml’s own perspective, are at the centre. The exhibition opened during the ORF Lange Nacht der Museen on 3 October 2026, when the artist also performed songs of his own. It is on view until 31 December 2026, on Fridays from 17:00 to 19:00. Preiml had already exhibited prints at the gallery in 2024.

name: Blinddate der Perspektiven
text_en: The association kultur.im.puls shows works by three graduates of the Freie Akademie der Bildenden Künste Kärnten in Klagenfurt: Inés Urach, Nicoline von Heyl and Roswitha Bucher-Sakowski. According to the organiser, the title “Blinddate der Perspektiven” (blind date of perspectives) refers to three separately developed positions meeting in one exhibition. Urach combines paper and paint in abstract pictures, von Heyl paints process-based works in mixed media, and Bucher-Sakowski paints figurative pictures in acrylic. The works hang in the daylit stairwell gallery of the Impuls Center; further works are on view in the stairwell of the Seeboden municipal office.

name: FRAGIL
text_en: The Kunstverein postWERK devotes its annual exhibition at the Dinzlschloss to fragility, within the theme “schwach • šibko • debole” of the Triennale IV Kärnten 2026. Members and guest artists from Austria, Germany, Slovenia and Iran show painting, photography, installation, literature and performance. According to the organiser the exhibition treats tenderness as a state of attention, not of weakness. The works deal with vulnerability in material and in people, with fragile ecosystems and with a shared future. On the ORF Long Night of Museums on 3 October 2026, Christina Clar and Phil Yaeger performed “Wieso wir uns wiegen”.

name: Universität Klagenfurt
text_en: The Universität Klagenfurt was founded in 1970. It has four faculties and 30 institutes, with more than 13,300 students. Its Institute of Instructional and School Development (Institut für Unterrichts- und Schulentwicklung) belongs to the Faculty of Cultural and Educational Sciences.

name: Kunstverein postWERK
text_en: The Kunstverein postWERK is a non-profit art association based in Villach, founded in 2012 by Dorothee Unkel, its honorary president. Barbara Ambrusch-Rapp has chaired it since January 2020. Members and guest artists show an annual exhibition on a yearly theme, in 2026 “FRAGIL” at the Dinzlschloss in Villach.
